Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G1223 and G3007; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:--without ceasing, continual.
BiblicalUsage: Adialeiptos is the adjective form — 'unceasing' or 'continual.' Paul uses it twice: once of the continual sorrow in his heart for his fellow Jews who have not believed, and once of his unceasing remembrance of Timothy in prayer. One word carries both his grief and his devotion, neither of them switched off.
TheologicalSignificance: This word is a footnote in the story, not a headline, and its value is in the sentence it completes rather than in itself; in this case, the verse is Romans 9:2.
